newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal funds to take 20-30 pct of derivatives.
newsitem.headline: Portugal funds to take 20-30 pct of derivatives.

text.p: Portugal's investment funds, authorised last week to invest in local derivatives, will eventually account for 20-30 percent of the market, a senior official said.

The chairman of the Portuguese Association of Investment Fund Management (APFIN) said the trend would be for the funds to take around the same percentage of business as in the underlying cash markets.

But the impact of the decision by the Financial Markets Committee (CMVM) would not be immediate with business in derivatives gradually picking up next year, Jose Carlos Maia told Reuters in an interview.
"Over the next year, the impact of the funds will begin to be felt," he said.
Maia said that he expected the weight of the funds in the cash markets to remain at around 20-30 percent.
Funds could already invest in derivatives markets abroad.
Maia said that the entry of domestic funds into the local derivatives market in Oporto could eventually attract foreign investment funds to the exchange.
